title: Closure steps preserve Hamiltonicity
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $\nu$ vertices, and suppose $H$ is obtained from $G$ by a finite sequence (possibly empty) of Bondy–Chvátal closure steps, each of which selects two distinct nonadjacent vertices whose degrees sum to at least $\nu$ and joins them by an edge. Then $G$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $H$ is Hamiltonian.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
H is reachable from G by the reflexive–transitive closure of the closure-step relation (a finite, possibly empty, sequence of closure steps)
each closure step adds an edge between two distinct nonadjacent vertices whose degree sum is at least the number of vertices
replaced:
Thm 4.4 (honest restatement): reachability by closure steps preserves hamiltonicity.

A simple graph is hamiltonian if and only if its closure is
hamiltonian.
